title: Dock Report: 720 Loaned NS Bags, Product Not Found

fields.organization: Prairie Ridge Health — Department of Pharmacy, Central Stockroom & Receiving
fields.location: Receiving dock (inbound bay) and central pharmacy stockroom entrance
fields.summary: At 09:35 a Webster Valley Medical Center courier dropped 60 cases of sodium chloride 1000 mL bags at our dock and left. At 09:40 the Webster Valley pharmacy buyer (515-555-0164) called Purchasing to say their director approved the loan: 60 cases × 12 = 720 bags, to be returned one for one within 30 days, and that the loan form was emailed for us to sign and send back. I counted the shipment and checked it against the packing slip. The cases are not our usual product: the labeler and label layout are different. The bag reads '0.9% Sodium Chloride Injection USP 1000 mL', NDC 0000-5678-10 (fictional), lot WV-88213, exp 03/2027. I scanned a test bag and the pharmacy system returned PRODUCT NOT FOUND, so it will not scan at the bedside or load into a cabinet pocket as is. The courier left a packing slip only. No signed loan agreement came with the shipment. At 09:41 the ICU called the stockroom asking to come pick up two cases now.

findings.notes: 60 cases counted, 12 bags per case, 720 bags. Matches the Webster Valley packing slip.
No crushed, wet or torn cases. Spot check of 6 bags: overwraps intact, no visible leaks.
Single lot WV-88213, exp 03/2027 on every case checked. Not the quarantined lot NS-26-0917A.

findings.item: Labeler / label layout vs. Prairie Ridge stock
findings.notes: Different manufacturer and label design from our NS 1000 mL. Wording reads '0.9% Sodium Chloride Injection USP' and the strength is placed differently on the face of the bag.
NDC 0000-5678-10 scanned at 09:38: PRODUCT NOT FOUND. No item record, no cabinet pocket mapping, no bedside barcode match.
Not received with the shipment. Buyer says the form was emailed to Purchasing. No Prairie Ridge signature on file at time of report.
Packing slip only. Lists quantity, NDC and lot. Nothing showing whose license covers the transfer.
Outside storeroom scope. The port design looks different from ours; a pharmacist needs to look at it.

actionsTaken: Counted all 60 cases against the packing slip at 09:36
Scanned one bag at 09:38: PRODUCT NOT FOUND
Left all 60 cases shrink-wrapped on the inbound bay, not put away and not received into inventory
Taped a 'HOLD — DO NOT DISTRIBUTE' sign on the pallet
Told the ICU caller at 09:41 that nothing ships until Purchasing releases it, and to call Purchasing at ext. 3612
Called Purchasing (ext. 3612) at 09:43 to report the shipment and the scan failure
recommendations: Purchasing / Director of Pharmacy: tell the stockroom whether these 720 bags go to a hold location or into stock, and when
Clinical pharmacy: look at the label, volume and bag port before anything goes to a unit
Pharmacy system: build an item record for NDC 0000-5678-10 before anyone tries to load cabinets
Do not count these 720 bags in the days-on-hand figure until someone signs for them
fields.photosNote: 5 photos attached: IMG_1005_01–05 (pallet on dock, case label, front of bag next to a Prairie Ridge NS 1000 mL bag, scanner screen showing PRODUCT NOT FOUND, packing slip)

instructorNote: This tests whether players hold the 720 loaned bags until the Director of Pharmacy has signed the loan agreement and the CPM/Medication Safety Officer has run the substitution checklist and built the NDC, instead of sending cases to the ICU. Watch whether the PIM leaves the bags out of days on hand until they are accepted, and then briefs the IC on whether they change the Wednesday deferral projection.
